info.title: Halo: Combat Evolved
info.author: thelinkin3000
info.description: Halo: Combat Evolved, built from the decompilation of the Xbox game. Needs your own disc image.
info.details:
NOTE: Halo's game data is not included. Put an Xbox disc image of Halo: Combat Evolved (any version, .iso or .xiso) on the SD card as /switch/halo/halo.iso; the game unpacks its maps folder from it on the first start (about 1.7 GB on the card, a few minutes). Or put the disc's maps folder at /switch/halo/maps yourself.

Halo: Combat Evolved on the Switch, built from the decompilation of the Xbox game: the campaign, split-screen and online multiplayer, Halo Custom Edition maps (in /switch/halo/custom_maps), gyro aiming, and the game's own renderer on deko3d at up to 1080p docked.

Saves go in /switch/halo/save and the settings in /switch/halo/config.toml. The game updates itself from its GitHub releases when a new build is out.

changelog:
vbuild-123
Build 123

- Main menu: the X button (Y on the Switch, Square on the PS5), or a tap on NEWS, opens the news: this release's notes in a window that scrolls. (thelinkin3000)
- PS5: Join Game > Direct Link shows a QR code: scan it with a phone (or open the address under it) and paste an invite link there, and the PS5 joins its game. The page is served on the local network only while Direct Link is open (network.link_page). (thelinkin3000)
- PS5: Server Setup's invite row opens the game's invite link as a QR code, for a phone to read; B closes it. (thelinkin3000)
- Bots drive and ride vehicles: a bot whose goal is far off takes an empty Warthog, Ghost or Scorpion, rides as a Warthog's gunner when a teammate drives, backs off when stuck, and mans turrets near an enemy (bots.vehicles). (thelinkin3000, from BirchWoodGod's halo-ce-vita)
- Bots go for health packs when hurt, and for an overshield or camouflage nearby. (thelinkin3000, from BirchWoodGod's halo-ce-vita)
- Bots hold vantage points: a bot with a sniper rifle or a rocket launcher (or a pistol in Slayer) holds a place overlooking the map a while, and leaves it when an enemy comes near, it runs low on ammunition, it is hurt, or its flag needs it. (thelinkin3000, from BirchWoodGod's halo-ce-vita)
- Bots find their way better: through teleporters when a goal cannot be walked to, through them as shortcuts when they save a long walk, and up ladders. (thelinkin3000, from BirchWoodGod's halo-ce-vita)
- Bots can spread over a map's side lanes instead of all going down the middle (bots.routes: direct, lanes or mixed). (thelinkin3000, from BirchWoodGod's halo-ce-vita)
- Switch and PS5: the server browser lists the master servers' dedicated servers, as the other platforms do. (thelinkin3000)

 From OpenCE
- Network version 39: this build plays with OpenCE 39 and later, not with Build 122 or older.
- The server browser has a DEDICATED tab for the master servers' dedicated servers, and opens on ALL GAMES, dedicated servers first.
- The server browser asks the official master server, master.opencommunityedition.com, when masters.txt names none.
- A server that refuses a player's name says so: "The host refused: your player name".
- Fishsticks and Recon controller layouts.
- The host refuses a reported hit with no line of sight to the target.
- Gun Game: the plasma rifle and plasma pistol can fire.
- A client keeps its inventory until its weapons have arrived, so it no longer spawns empty-handed.

Build: https://github.com/thelinkin3000/halo-ce-universal/actions/runs/40359610187

The release builds are for playing; the debug builds stop at the first failed assertion and log it.

Build 111
- Switch and PS5: the main menu has no QUIT: the console's own Home or PS button leaves the game.
- PS5: each build has its own version number on the console, so stores and the console can tell that a newer build is an update.

Build 110
- Switch and Android: Halo's loading screen draws, the light sweeping over the Xbox's picture with its glowing trail; maps extracted by earlier builds get the picture from the disc image at the next start (on every platform).
- Switch: the first seconds after starting no longer freeze or cut the music, and the menus appear whole once their shaders are ready, behind the loading screen.
- Switch: when it looks for an update, the Switch also downloads the shaders of the campaign and of every multiplayer map (the shared shader keys), so a console compiles them in the background from its first start instead of as each map is first played.
- Switch: a map's load waits for its shaders under the loading screen, ten seconds at most, so a level's first moments are drawn whole; the loading screen's light now sweeps across the whole wait. Going back to the menus after a level no longer waits four seconds.
- Switch, Android and PS5: maps load sooner: the map is read from the card while it is unpacked (a campaign level about two seconds sooner on the Switch).
- Android and PS5: no more objects missing for the first frames of a map or a new effect: shaders compile on all the cores but two, and a draw whose shader is not ready compiles it itself, for up to a frame's time each frame.
